jobs.description:
Role Overview

The Procurement Coordinator supports the day-to-day operations of the Procurement function by coordinating procurement activities, maintaining procurement systems and records, supporting contract administration, monitoring compliance, and assisting with supplier and service provider onboarding activities.

This role partners closely with Procurement, Finance, Legal, Program Operations, and external suppliers to support CAA’s mission and EPR program operations through efficient, compliant and stakeholder focused procurement processes

Key Responsibilities

Procurement Operations & Governance

  • Support procurement intake and workflow management across multiple state programs.
  • Assist stakeholders with procurement policies, procedures, and purchasing requirements.
  • Monitor procurement requests to ensure compliance with organizational policies and approval requirements.
  • Maintain procurement documentation, records, and audit-ready files.
  • Identify opportunities to streamline procurement processes and improve user experience.
  • Support implementation and maintenance of procurement standard operating procedures, job aids, and knowledge base resources.

Contract Administration

  • Support contract intake, routing, execution, and repository management activities.
  • Maintain contract records and monitor contract expiration and renewal dates.
  • Coordinate with Legal, Procurement, and business stakeholders to ensure contract documentation is complete.
  • Assist with contract reporting and repository accuracy.

Reporting & Analytics

  • Support the collection, maintenance, and validation of procurement data used for reporting and analytics.
  • Assist with maintaining procurement records and operational data to support reporting and compliance activities.
  • Maintain procurement data and reporting tools.
  • Support internal audits and data requests.

Supplier Support & Onboarding

  • Provide support to the Procurement Specialist in supplier onboarding activities.
  • Assist with collection and validation of supplier documentation.
  • Support supplier banking verification processes and onboarding workflows as needed.
  • Serve as backup support for supplier onboarding during periods of increased volume or team absences.
  • Track onboarding status and communicate progress to internal stakeholders.

Stakeholder Engagement

  • Serve as a liaison between Procurement, Finance, Legal, Program Operations, and suppliers.
  • Proactively follow up on open requests to help ensure stakeholders and suppliers receive timely updates.
  • Respond to procurement-related inquiries and provide guidance on established processes (templates, job aids, and knowledge base resources.).
  • Support procurement training sessions, office hours, and communication initiatives.
  • Assist with special projects and strategic initiatives.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Skills & Competencies

  • Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Teams.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in Business Administration, Procurement, Supply Chain, Finance, or a related field or 7+ years related experience.
  • 2+ years of experience in procurement, purchasing, contract administration, supplier management, finance operations, or related administrative support.
  • Experience working within ERP systems such as Workday, SAP, Oracle, or similar platforms.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Teams.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience supporting procure-to-pay (P2P) processes.
  • Experience with supplier onboarding and vendor management.
  • Experience with contract lifecycle management systems such as Ironclad.
  • Experience with procurement reporting, KPI development, and compliance monitoring.
  • Experience working in a nonprofit, regulated, or multi-state operating environment.
  • Familiarity with Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) regulations, Producer Responsibility Organizations (PRO)s), or environmental compliance programs.

Compensation & Other Information

Location:Remote in the United States of America; Preference for candidates in the Cincinnati, OH or Atlanta, GA areas to support collaboration and periodic in-person engagement.

  • Travel: Occasional travel may be required for team offsites, stakeholder meetings, or organizational planning sessions.
  • Pay Rate: Based on a variety of factors in accordance with applicable law including the successful candidate’s relevant experience, skills, knowledge, and experience.
  • Reports To: Procurement Director, Finance and Accounting

jobs.excerpt: About BJAKThe original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money.
jobs.description:
About BJAK

The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

The Role

We are looking for a Lead Engineer to take technical ownership of complex products and systems and raise the engineering bar across the team.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You will be expected to design systems, write and review code, solve difficult engineering problems, guide other engineers and drive major initiatives from idea to production.

You should be comfortable moving between architecture and implementation — making strong technical decisions while still being close enough to the code to execute when needed.

What You'll Own

  • Lead the technical design and execution of major products, features and engineering initiatives.

  • Design scalable, reliable and maintainable systems across backend, frontend, APIs, databases and infrastructure.

  • Stay hands-on with engineering through coding, prototyping, code reviews, debugging and production problem-solving.

  • Make architecture decisions and technical trade-offs that balance speed, scalability, reliability and maintainability.

  • Break ambiguous product and technical problems into clear engineering solutions and execution plans.

  • Set a high bar for code quality, system design, testing, security, observability and production reliability.

  • Review technical designs and code from other engineers and provide clear, actionable feedback.

  • Mentor engineers and help strengthen technical capability across the team.

  • Identify technical risks, bottlenecks and architectural weaknesses before they become larger problems.

  • Work closely with engineering, product, design and AI teams to ship high-quality products quickly.

  • Improve engineering tooling, development practices and automation to increase team velocity.

  • Own systems beyond release — monitor production, investigate incidents, resolve root causes and continuously improve reliability.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong software engineering background with significant experience building and shipping production systems.

  • Deep technical expertise in one or more areas such as backend, frontend, distributed systems, APIs, databases or cloud infrastructure.

  • Strong system design and architecture skills with experience making technical decisions for complex or high-scale systems.

  • Strong coding ability and willingness to remain hands-on.

  • Proven experience leading major engineering projects or providing technical leadership to other engineers.

  • Comfortable reviewing code, debugging complex issues and working directly with production systems.

  • Able to explain complex technical decisions clearly and influence engineers across teams.

  • Strong product sense and ability to connect technical decisions to customer and business outcomes.

  • Able to work fast with ambiguity and take ownership from problem definition through production.

  • Strong judgment around when to move quickly, when to simplify and when deeper engineering investment is required.

This Role Is Not For

  • Engineers who want a leadership title but no longer want to write or review code.

  • People who only want to work within one narrow technical area.

  • Engineers who wait for complete specifications before starting.

  • Candidates who over-engineer solutions when a simpler approach would achieve the outcome.

  • Engineers who focus only on implementation without understanding the product or business problem.

  • People who avoid production incidents, difficult debugging or ownership after release.

  • Candidates who make vague claims about technical leadership without being able to explain what they personally designed, built, shipped or scaled.

The Bar

We are looking for technical leaders with real engineering career highlights.

A strong highlight is not simply having a senior title or working at a famous technology company. A strong highlight means you personally designed, built, shipped or scaled a serious product, platform or system and can go deep into the technical decisions behind it.

You should be able to demonstrate both technical depth and technical leadership — someone who can solve difficult engineering problems personally while making the engineers around them stronger.

Location

This is a remote role. We hire globally and work across multiple countries and time zones.

Candidates should be comfortable working effectively in a distributed, fast-moving international team and collaborating with colleagues across different locations.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Technical interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

jobs.description:
Job Title: AVP, Application Security

Job Location: Work at Home, Rhode Island, United States

Job Location Type: Remote

Job Contract Type: Full time

Job Seniority Level:

We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.

Position Summary

CVS Health is seeking a polished and experienced security leader to serve as Associate Vice President of Application Security, responsible for defining and executing the enterprise strategy for securing software across its full development lifecycle. This role owns the policies, technical standards, and tooling that enable CVS Health's engineering teams to build and deploy secure applications at scale. The AVP will lead a high-performing team of application security engineers and architects, partner deeply with Developer Experience leadership to embed security seamlessly into agile development practices and serve as a trusted advisor to executive stakeholders on software security risk. This leader will balance targeted security outcomes with developer productivity, ensuring that security is an enabler — not a barrier — to innovation.

Key Responsibilities:

Strategic Leadership

  • Define and own the enterprise application security strategy, roadmap, and policy framework, aligned with CVS Health's business objectives and regulatory obligations.
  • Establish and enforce technical standards for secure software development, including code scanning, code vulnerability management, and secure-by-design principles.
  • Serve as a subject matter expert and trusted advisor to senior technology and business executives on emerging application security risks, attack trends, and industry best practices.
  • Drive continuous improvement across the application security program through metrics, benchmarking, and innovation.

Application Security Engineering & Controls

  • Secure Development Lifecycle (SDLC) Integration: Lead the integration of application security scanning, testing, and policy enforcement gates into CI/CD pipelines across the enterprise. Partner with Developer Experience leadership to ensure security tooling is frictionless, developer-friendly, and compatible with agile delivery practices.
  • Static Application Security Testing (SAST): Define strategy, standards, and tooling for enterprise-wide SAST scanning. Manage tuning of rulesets to reduce false positives, drive remediation workflows, and ensure coverage across all critical code repositories.
  • Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST): Oversee DAST program covering pre-production and production environments. Establish automated scanning schedules, triage processes, and integration with enterprise vulnerability management platforms.
  • Web Application Firewall (WAF) Management: Own the strategy, configuration, and operations of the enterprise WAF platform. Define and maintain rule sets, monitor for emerging threats, and ensure alignment with zero-trust and defense-in-depth principles.
  • Code Repository Scanning: Implement and manage continuous scanning of source code repositories for secrets, misconfigurations, exposed credentials, and policy violations. Establish guardrails and automated enforcement to prevent insecure code from reaching production.
  • AI-Assisted Code Generation Security: Develop policies and technical controls to assess and govern security risks introduced by AI-assisted code generation tools (e.g., GitHub Copilot, generative AI coding assistants). Define standards for safe use and implement scanning capabilities to detect AI-generated code vulnerabilities.
  • Third-Party and Open-Source Software (SCA) Scanning: Manage the Software Composition Analysis (SCA) program to identify and remediate vulnerabilities in third-party libraries and open-source dependencies. Maintain visibility into the software supply chain and drive compliance with internal ingestion policies.
  • Content Delivery Network (CDN) Security Management: Oversee security configuration and policy enforcement for content delivery network infrastructure. Ensure CDN-layer protections — including DDoS mitigation, bot management, and TLS standards — are aligned with enterprise security policy.
  • Application Security Technology Stack: Own the full application security tooling portfolio. Manage vendor relationships, licensing, platform health, and roadmap alignment. Evaluate and introduce emerging technologies to improve coverage, automation, and developer experience.

Governance & Compliance

  • Define and maintain application security policies, standards, and operational procedures.
  • Ensure compliance with applicable regulatory frameworks and industry standards, including HIPAA, PCI-DSS, CCPA, NIST SSDF, and OWASP.
  • Provide executive-level reporting and governance dashboards that communicate program health, risk posture, and remediation progress.
  • Establish and maintain a risk-based vulnerability management process focused specifically on software development vulnerabilities, including those introduced through code, dependencies, and the build and deployment pipeline, in partnership with peer security organizations.

Leadership & Collaboration

  • Build, lead, and develop a high-performing team of application security engineers, architects, and program managers.
  • Partner closely with Developer Experience leadership to align security tooling and practices with developer workflows, ensuring security is integrated seamlessly into agile and DevSecOps pipelines.
  • Collaborate with Cyber Defense, Data Protection, Infrastructure Security, Legal, Compliance, and Technology leadership to deliver integrated security outcomes.
  • Partner with Chief Data and Technology Officers (CDTOs) across CVS Health business units to understand technology strategies, influence security-targeted outcomes, and ensure application security priorities are embedded within divisional roadmaps and investment decisions.
  • Foster a security-minded engineering culture through developer education, secure coding training, security champion programs, and engagement with engineering communities of practice.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs):

  • Pipeline Coverage: Percentage of active software development pipelines with integrated SAST, DAST, and SCA scanning controls.
  • Vulnerability Remediation SLA: Mean time to remediate (MTTR) critical and high application security vulnerabilities, tracked against defined SLAs.
  • Secrets & Policy Violations: Reduction in secrets exposed in code repositories and policy violations detected year-over-year.
  • WAF Effectiveness: Percentage of malicious web traffic blocked; reduction in application-layer incidents attributed to WAF-protected assets.
  • Third-Party Risk Coverage: Percentage of production applications with up-to-date SCA coverage and no unaddressed critical open-source vulnerabilities.
  • AI Code Security: Coverage rate of AI-assisted code generation under security policy and scanning controls.
  • Developer Experience Satisfaction: Developer NPS and feedback scores related to security tooling and friction within the SDLC.
  • Regulatory Compliance: Audit findings related to application security controls, targeting zero critical findings.
  • Program Adoption: Number of development teams operating under the secure SDLC framework and security champion program.
  • Roadmap Delivery: On-time completion of strategic application security initiatives and tooling milestones.

Required Qualifications

  • 12+ years of progressive experience in information security, with at least 5 years in application security leadership roles.
  • Deep technical background in software development, including hands-on coding experience in one or more modern programming languages (e.g., Java, Python, Go, JavaScript, or similar). Candidates must bring developer-level fluency to credibly engage with engineering teams, evaluate code-level risks, and drive meaningful secure coding practices.
  • Demonstrated expertise in application security engineering and secure software development lifecycle (SDLC) practices, grounded in first-hand experience building or shipping software.
  • Strong understanding of software architecture patterns, CI/CD pipelines, containerization, and cloud-native development — with the ability to assess security implications at every layer of the stack.
  • Hands-on experience managing enterprise application security tooling, including SAST, DAST, SCA, WAF, and repository scanning platforms.
  • Deep knowledge of application security standards and frameworks, including OWASP Top 10, NIST SSDF, and relevant regulatory requirements (HIPAA, PCI-DSS, CCPA).
  • Proven ability to influence engineering culture and drive security adoption at scale within agile development environments.
  • Strong leadership skills with experience building and managing cross-functional technical teams and influencing senior stakeholders.
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills; ability to translate complex security concepts for both technical and non-technical audiences.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Advanced degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or a related field.
  • Certifications such as CISSP, CSSLP, CISM, GWEB, or equivalent.
  • Experience in healthcare or other highly regulated industries.
  • Familiarity with AI/ML-driven security tooling and modern cloud-native application security architectures.
  • Experience implementing security programs within large-scale DevOps or platform engineering organizations.

Education

Bachelor's Degree

Pay Range

The typical pay range for this role is:

$185,400.00 - $375,950.00

This pay range represents the base hourly rate or base annual full-time salary for all positions in the job grade within which this position falls. The actual base salary offer will depend on a variety of factors including experience, education, geography and other relevant factors. This position is eligible for a CVS Health bonus, commission or short-term incentive program in addition to the base pay range listed above. This position also includes an award target in the company’s equity award program.

Our people fuel our future. Our teams reflect the customers, patients, members and communities we serve and we are committed to fostering a workplace where every colleague feels valued and that they belong.

Great benefits for great people

We take pride in offering a comprehensive and competitive mix of pay and benefits that reflects our commitment to our colleagues and their families.

This full‑time position is eligible for a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the physical, emotional, and financial well‑being of colleagues and their families. The benefits for this position include medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid time off, retirement savings options, wellness programs, and other resources, based on eligibility.

Additional details about available benefits are provided during the application process and on Benefits Moments.

jobs.description:
Senior Product Manager — Manifest

About Manifest

Manifest is building modern software for the tours and activities industry.

Our customers run real-world businesses: tours, attractions, experiences, rentals, and activities. They need software that helps them sell more, operate smoothly, and deliver great guest experiences.

We're building a B2B2C SaaS platform that brings booking, ecommerce, payments, accounting, operations, and customer experience together in a modern architecture. The product surface is broad, the workflows are nuanced, and the opportunity is big. That surface now spans several distinct product areas, including a newer, AI-native platform for building and delivering customer websites end-to-end. We're hiring more than one Senior Product Manager, and we'll match each hire to the area where their strengths fit best, from established features to fast-moving, zero-to-one greenfield work.

We're looking for Senior Product Managers to own product direction, roadmap, and prioritization for one or more key areas of Manifest.

This is not a backlog management role. We're looking for someone who can take ambiguous customer and business problems, find the shape of the opportunity, make smart tradeoffs, and help a cross-functional team ship high-quality product experiences.

About the Role

As a Senior Product Manager, you'll turn customer insight, business context, and technical possibilities into clear product direction and own the delivery end-to-end.

Modern product work is changing, and this role reflects that. We expect our PMs to be fluent and genuinely enthusiastic users of AI-assisted tools—using Claude, Cursor, v0, and similar tools to explore interactions, build lightweight prototypes, and make product ideas concrete before implementation begins. On some of our teams, AI-native workflows are not just a way of working faster; they're central to the product itself.

You'll work closely with Product leadership, Engineering, customer-facing teams, and design-minded front-end engineers. Depending on the area you own, there may not be a dedicated product designer, so you should be comfortable playing an active role in shaping user workflows, interaction patterns, and overall product quality.

You'll also be the bridge between executive vision and execution: taking high-level direction set by our leadership team and honing it into concrete, buildable product requirements. Leadership helps frame the why and the what, but you own the product decisions about what to build and how to bring it to life.

You do not need to be a front-end engineer, and you won't be expected to write production code. But strong technical fluency is a real advantage—enough to collaborate deeply with engineers on UI-heavy, technically nuanced product areas, and to understand the systems you're shaping. A technical or former engineering background is strongly preferred.

You should also be comfortable owning the delivery side of the work, along with the product vision, like milestones, sequencing, and keeping a small team moving.

What You'll Do

  • Own roadmap, prioritization, delivery, and product outcomes for one or more areas of Manifest
  • Develop a deep understanding of our customers, their businesses, and the tours and activities industry
  • Lead discovery with customers, internal stakeholders, support teams, sales, customer success, and go-to-market partners
  • Translate customer problems, business goals, and operational complexity into clear product direction
  • Define product requirements, success metrics, release scope, and tradeoffs
  • Partner closely with engineering to shape pragmatic, high-quality solutions, and help sequence and drive delivery
  • Work closely with front-end engineers on user flows, interaction details, edge cases, and product polish
  • Use AI-assisted tools, lightweight prototypes, wireframes, diagrams, and sketches to clarify product ideas and reduce ambiguity
  • Help raise the bar for UX quality, including in areas without a dedicated Product Designer
  • Create clear product artifacts: problem statements, opportunity briefs, product specs, workflow diagrams, acceptance criteria, launch plans, and release notes
  • Balance customer value, business impact, technical constraints, and delivery realities
  • Communicate product direction clearly across Product, Engineering, Customer Success, Sales, Marketing, and leadership
  • Collaborate with Product leadership on strategy while taking ownership of day-to-day product execution

What We're Looking For

  • Significant Product Management experience, ideally in a B2B or B2B2C SaaS environment
  • A track record of owning roadmap, prioritization, and delivery for meaningful product areas
  • Strong product judgment: you can move from ambiguous problems to coherent product direction
  • Strong written communication and the ability to create clear, actionable product specs
  • A measurement-driven approach to product, defining success metrics up front and proving the impact of changes quantitatively
  • Fluency and enthusiasm for AI-assisted product work using tools like Claude, Cursor, v0, Figma, or FigJam to prototype, explore, and communicate ideas
  • A technical background, former engineering experience, or strong technical fluency; enough to understand the product deeply and partner closely with engineers on technically nuanced, UI-heavy areas
  • Comfort owning delivery and project execution on small teams alongside product vision
  • Experience leading discovery, evaluating opportunities, and making thoughtful tradeoffs
  • Strong UX instincts and an eye for product quality, usability, workflow design, and polish
  • Familiarity with modern front-end patterns, design systems, HTML, CSS, or component-based product development
  • Experience with complex workflows, operational tools, booking flows, ecommerce, marketplaces, or other transaction-heavy SaaS products
  • Ability to operate effectively in ambiguity and bring structure to undefined problems, including in zero-to-one / startup-mode environments
  • A pragmatic, collaborative operating style

Nice to Have

  • Experience in travel, tourism, activities, hospitality, reservations, ecommerce, or booking platforms
  • Experience working on developer-adjacent products or platforms
  • Experience in a scale-up environment where product, design, and engineering responsibilities are highly collaborative
  • A track record of using AI tools to accelerate product discovery, prototyping, analysis, or specification in a real production setting
  • Experience with analytics, experimentation, funnel optimization, SEO, or conversion-focused product work

How We Work

We move quickly, but we care about craft.

Manifest serves users with complex day-to-day workflows, so product quality matters. We care about whether the product makes sense, whether the workflow is intuitive, whether the edge cases are handled thoughtfully, and whether the experience feels modern and trustworthy.

We value product managers who are curious, direct, clear-thinking, and outcome-oriented. We are not looking for someone who simply collects requirements or manages tickets. We're looking for someone who can understand customer problems, shape direction, make tradeoffs, and partner with Engineering from ambiguity through delivery and iteration.

At GoTo, we care about helping our people succeed at work and feel supported in life. Our employee benefits and programs are designed to support your well-being, growth, and sense of belonging. Here's what you can expect as part of our team:

jobs.description:
Please note that we are unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position.

Recruiting agencies: Proper Voltage does not accept unsolicited candidate submissions. Please do not contact any employees directly unless you have an existing engagement with the company.

About Proper Voltage

Proper Voltage is unlocking the next generation of battery technology across robotics, data centers, and defense.

We're building intelligent battery systems that make advanced chemistries (sodium-ion, lithium-titanate, lithium-silicon) work in products that were never designed for them. Humanoid robots can upgrade power systems without redesigning their entire platform. Data centers get safer, cheaper backup power. Drones and autonomous vehicles get higher energy density without lengthy integration cycles.

If you want to work on hard engineering problems that matter this is the place.

Job Overview

The NPI Prototype Procurement Manager owns fast-turn prototype sourcing during new product development. When engineering needs a part quoted and built in days, not weeks, this role makes it happen, and makes sure the part we source for a prototype build doesn't quietly become a bad default for production.

This role reports to the Director of Supply Chain and works closely with engineering, our prototype contract manufacturers, and our production sourcing team. Prototype CMs are good at turning parts fast; they are not set up to decide which of those parts should become a real production supplier, or to catch when a rushed sourcing decision is costing us on markup or quality risk down the line. That decision needs a dedicated owner on our side.

We are building this role now because the gap is already showing up in real costs: parts moving slower than they should, and markups on prototype-CM-sourced parts that we're paying today without anyone tracking whether that's the right long-term call.

Scope

Fast-turn sourcing: for parts that are strategic, long-lead, or clearly headed toward production, you run the RFQ and sourcing decision directly rather than letting a prototype CM default-source it under time pressure.

Prototype-to-production tracking: for parts a prototype CM sources on our behalf, you track what was bought, from whom, and at what cost, and you flag early which of those should transition to a qualified production supplier instead of carrying forward by default.

Cost visibility: you own should-cost tracking on new parts as designs stabilize, flagging anything trending over target early enough to actually do something about it.

This role sits specifically in the handoff between early prototype builds and production. Production commodity strategy, supplier negotiation, and cost-out on qualified production parts stay with our sourcing team. Day-to-day material tracking and expediting once a part is in production stays with our materials team. This role owns the messy middle: prototype-stage sourcing decisions that determine what production inherits.

This role starts as an individual contributor working in close partnership with engineering.

Who this role is for

You have direct experience sourcing prototype and early-production parts in a hardware environment, working shoulder to shoulder with engineering while designs are still moving. You're comfortable quoting and placing an order on a part that might change again next week.

You think past the next build. When a prototype shop sources a part fast, you're the person asking whether that supplier, that price, and that quality level are good enough to carry into production, or whether it needs to change before it's too late to change cheaply.

You're comfortable working through and around a contract manufacturer's own sourcing team rather than owning a factory floor yourself. You know how to get a CM's buyer to move fast for you, and you know when to route around them and source directly.

You have a cost-conscious streak. You notice when a markup looks high and you're willing to do the work to find out if it's justified.

You are comfortable in early-stage environments where the playbook is still being written, and where this specific handoff between prototype and production sourcing hasn't had a dedicated owner before.

This role is not a fit for

  • You are looking to own production commodity strategy or long-term supplier negotiation. That sits with our sourcing team.
  • You are looking to own day-to-day material tracking and expediting once parts are in production. That sits with our materials team.
  • You need stable designs and a locked BOM to work effectively. This role lives in the period before that’s true.
  • You would find a startup operating tempo frustrating.

What you'll do

Prototype sourcing

  • Run quick-turn RFQs and place orders directly for strategic, long-lead, or clearly production-bound parts during prototype builds.
  • Partner with engineering embedded in design reviews and build planning, understanding what’s changing and what’s stabilizing.
  • Manage supplier relationships for quick-turn shops separate from our production supplier base.

Prototype-to-production handoff

  • Track every part sourced by a prototype CM on our behalf: supplier, cost, and whether it’s fit to carry forward.
  • Flag parts that should transition to a qualified production supplier early enough to make the change before it’s expensive.
  • Hand off qualified parts and supplier context cleanly to our production sourcing team, with a clear paper trail rather than tribal knowledge.

Cost visibility

  • Own should-cost tracking on new parts as designs stabilize, flagging cost overruns early.
  • Identify where prototype CM markups are worth the convenience and where a direct sourcing decision would save real money.

Cross-functional partnership

  • Partner with our production sourcing team on the handoff for parts moving from prototype to production.
  • Partner with our materials team on build timing and part availability during prototype phases.
  • Partner with engineering on design-for-sourcing input while parts are still changeable.

Required Qualifications

  • 4+ years in procurement or sourcing supporting new product development in a hardware or industrial product environment.
  • Direct experience with fast-turn/quick-turn sourcing (rapid prototyping shops, quick-turn machining or fab, low-volume electronics).
  • Comfort working alongside a contract manufacturer’s own sourcing team rather than owning a factory floor directly.
  • Experience evaluating whether a prototype-sourced part or supplier is fit to carry into production.
  • Ability to operate independently and build process where none exists yet.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in battery, energy storage, power electronics, or other hardware-adjacent categories.
  • Should-cost or cost estimation experience on early-stage or immature designs.
  • Experience transitioning parts from a prototype or contract manufacturer to a qualified production supplier.
  • Early-stage startup experience.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Base salary of $155,000 to $175,000, plus equity.
  • Health, dental, and vision insurance.
  • Flexible PTO with a generous holiday policy.
  • Carlsbad, CA strongly preferred. Open to fully remote for the right candidate. Occasional travel to contract manufacturers.

Ready to work on power systems that matter? Let's talk.

jobs.description:
About BJAK

The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

The Role

We are looking for a Lead Engineer to take technical ownership of complex products and systems and raise the engineering bar across the team.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You will be expected to design systems, write and review code, solve difficult engineering problems, guide other engineers and drive major initiatives from idea to production.

You should be comfortable moving between architecture and implementation — making strong technical decisions while still being close enough to the code to execute when needed.

What You'll Own

  • Lead the technical design and execution of major products, features and engineering initiatives.

  • Design scalable, reliable and maintainable systems across backend, frontend, APIs, databases and infrastructure.

  • Stay hands-on with engineering through coding, prototyping, code reviews, debugging and production problem-solving.

  • Make architecture decisions and technical trade-offs that balance speed, scalability, reliability and maintainability.

  • Break ambiguous product and technical problems into clear engineering solutions and execution plans.

  • Set a high bar for code quality, system design, testing, security, observability and production reliability.

  • Review technical designs and code from other engineers and provide clear, actionable feedback.

  • Mentor engineers and help strengthen technical capability across the team.

  • Identify technical risks, bottlenecks and architectural weaknesses before they become larger problems.

  • Work closely with engineering, product, design and AI teams to ship high-quality products quickly.

  • Improve engineering tooling, development practices and automation to increase team velocity.

  • Own systems beyond release — monitor production, investigate incidents, resolve root causes and continuously improve reliability.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong software engineering background with significant experience building and shipping production systems.

  • Deep technical expertise in one or more areas such as backend, frontend, distributed systems, APIs, databases or cloud infrastructure.

  • Strong system design and architecture skills with experience making technical decisions for complex or high-scale systems.

  • Strong coding ability and willingness to remain hands-on.

  • Proven experience leading major engineering projects or providing technical leadership to other engineers.

  • Comfortable reviewing code, debugging complex issues and working directly with production systems.

  • Able to explain complex technical decisions clearly and influence engineers across teams.

  • Strong product sense and ability to connect technical decisions to customer and business outcomes.

  • Able to work fast with ambiguity and take ownership from problem definition through production.

  • Strong judgment around when to move quickly, when to simplify and when deeper engineering investment is required.

This Role Is Not For

  • Engineers who want a leadership title but no longer want to write or review code.

  • People who only want to work within one narrow technical area.

  • Engineers who wait for complete specifications before starting.

  • Candidates who over-engineer solutions when a simpler approach would achieve the outcome.

  • Engineers who focus only on implementation without understanding the product or business problem.

  • People who avoid production incidents, difficult debugging or ownership after release.

  • Candidates who make vague claims about technical leadership without being able to explain what they personally designed, built, shipped or scaled.

The Bar

We are looking for technical leaders with real engineering career highlights.

A strong highlight is not simply having a senior title or working at a famous technology company. A strong highlight means you personally designed, built, shipped or scaled a serious product, platform or system and can go deep into the technical decisions behind it.

You should be able to demonstrate both technical depth and technical leadership — someone who can solve difficult engineering problems personally while making the engineers around them stronger.

Location

This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our local office at least 3 days per week, with the remaining days offering flexibility to work remotely.

Candidates should be based in, or able to work from, the location where the role is advertised.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Technical interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Marketing & Communications
jobs.excerpt: About TaprootTaproot Foundation is a national nonprofit powering the next generation of pro bono service.
jobs.description:
About Taproot

Taproot Foundation is a national nonprofit powering the next generation of pro bono service. For more than 20 years, we’ve connected nonprofits with high-quality, high-trust support from skilled professionals—so they can meet urgent challenges, grow their impact, and lead with confidence.

Today, we’re expanding that vision. We’re innovating our platform, deepening partnerships, and shaping a future-focused pro bono marketplace. Our aim: a system that meets nonprofit needs with ease, speed, and excellence—lowering barriers to access, centering community voices, and embracing innovation, including AI.

The Opportunity

The Senior Manager, Marketing & Communications is the campaign strategist and executor at the center of Taproot’s marketing engine. Reporting to the Head of Marketing & Communications, this role turns strategy into finished work: campaigns planned and delivered, content written, social channels growing, and launches carried to the finish line in service of Taproot’s bold vision to build the next-generation pro bono marketplace.

The Head of Marketing & Communications sets where the function is going. The Senior Manager takes a mandate, such as a campaign around a signature event or a flagship research release, shapes the strategy, builds the plan, and leads it through to delivery. This person is a maker at heart who loves producing the work, brings the independence to carry a project from hand-off through to the finish, and serves as an engaged thought partner who pushes thinking and offers input, with clear accountability for execution.

This role carries particular ambition for Taproot’s social media presence: someone who sees social as a channel that can shape action at the movement level, takes differentiated content approaches based on social platform, and who will modernize and evolve Taproot’s presence into new platforms and formats where the next generation of pro bono talent is ready to be engaged. A tech-forward mindset runs throughout, with curiosity about emerging tools, including AI, to expand reach, speed, and quality.

Reports to the Head of Marketing & Communications, with significant accountability for campaign execution and day to day marketing and communication operations. This role has no direct reports. Works across Programs, Strategic Partnerships & Advancement, Product, Finance, and Executive Leadership to align delivery with organizational priorities. Directs the work of contracted design and production partners, and interfaces with partners and sector collaborators in support of campaigns and convenings.

Key Responsibilities

Campaign Strategy, Planning & Execution

  • Develop the campaign strategy for Taproot's priority initiatives, such as the brand refresh activation, the 25th Anniversary campaign, or a flagship research release, translating the marketing strategy into audiences, objectives, channels, sequencing, and measurement.

  • Lead two to three signature campaigns each year from plan to delivery, producing and coordinating work across channels.

  • Maintain a rolling 6-12-month campaign calendar aligned to narrative priorities, resourcing realities, and organizational milestones.

  • Develop briefs that give colleagues, contractors, and agency partners clear direction, sequencing, and success criteria.

  • Partner with Programs, Strategic Partnerships & Advancement, and Product on launch planning and on materials that help colleagues share Taproot’s message consistently.

Content Creation, Storytelling & Brand Activation

  • Write the work: campaign copy, email and web content, the stories behind research reports and case studies, and materials that support executive visibility.

  • Carry Taproot’s refreshed voice with a contemporary, professional standard across every channel and format.

  • Bring vision and ambition to Taproot’s social media, growing our presence beyond LinkedIn into platforms and formats, such as Instagram and TikTok, where the next generation of pro bono consultants is ready to be engaged.

  • Create sharp, compelling social content made for each platform, experimenting with formats, trends, and emerging tools, and using simple measurement to show what is working.

  • Partner with Programs to source and shape stories that show the human impact of skilled service.

  • Hold a high-quality bar for clarity, craft, and brand consistency across the team’s output.

Design Direction, Performance & Delivery

  • Direct contracted design capacity: scope, brief, art-direct, and review design work to a contemporary, distinctive visual standard.

  • Ensure consistent application of Taproot’s refreshed brand across campaigns, channels, and materials.

  • Manage contractors and freelancers for surge capacity, keeping high-frequency, brand-critical work in-house.

  • Track and report campaign and channel performance, delivering clear summaries of what is working and what comes next.

  • Keep the briefs, workflows, and planning rhythms that make delivery predictable and efficient for a lean team.

Other Duties

  • Perform other duties as assigned to support Taproot’s marketing, communications, and organizational priorities.

This role requires occasional travel (up to 15%), as needed.

Requirements

Competencies Needed for Role:

  • Campaign Execution Leadership: Proven ability to build and deliver integrated, multi-channel campaigns end to end, carrying work from mandate to finish.

  • Exceptional Writing: A skilled, versatile writer who produces polished work across formats and carries a brand voice with consistency and craft.

  • Social Media Vision: Deep fluency in social platforms and formats, with sharp instincts for each platform and a conviction that social can shape action at the movement level.

  • Design Direction & Visual Judgment: Directs design work to a high visual standard, with a sharp eye for contemporary, distinctive brand expression.

  • Independent Ownership & Initiative: Self-directed; takes a mandate and moves it to done, anticipating needs ahead of the ask.

  • Strategic Contribution: Engages with strategy as a thought partner, pushes thinking, and translates direction into plans colleagues can act on.

  • Values-Driven Leadership: Deep belief in Taproot’s values of Pragmatic Optimism, Impact Orientation, Playful Professionalism, and Progress, with commitment to equity and inclusion.

Qualifications

  • 7-10 years of marketing and communications experience, including hands-on ownership of multi-channel campaigns from plan through delivery.

  • Experience in a startup, high-growth, or otherwise scrappy and resource-lean environment, comfortable producing the work directly rather than delegating it.

  • A strong, versatile writer across campaign copy, email, web, and social, with the range to shape the narrative behind research reports and case studies.

  • Demonstrated social media fluency, with platform-native content and strategy across channels such as LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, and short-form video.

  • Experience directing contractors, freelancers, or agency partners: scoping, briefing, art-directing, and reviewing work to a consistent quality and brand standard.

  • A data-informed approach, using metrics and audience insight to prioritize, optimize, and show what is working.

  • Fluency with digital tools and genuine curiosity about emerging ones, including AI, to expand reach, speed, and quality.

  • Self-directed and accountable, able to take a mandate and carry it to done while anticipating what the work needs.

  • Direct experience with or exposure to product marketing is preferred.

  • Nonprofit experience is welcome but not required. We are equally interested in candidates bringing startup, agency, or corporate marketing backgrounds.

Salary

Starting salary range is $90,000 - $105,000 per year. Exact placement within the range is based on location and experience.

To Apply

Please submit your resume and response to the application questions.

Apply through the Taproot Careers Page, not through a third-party website. We will review applications and interview promising candidates on a rolling basis.

We know great candidates may not meet every qualification. If this role excites you, we hope you’ll apply.

Taproot is deeply committed to advancing diversity, equity, and inclusion in everything we do—from the work we lead to the culture we’re building. We believe that diverse teams and inclusive partnerships are essential to driving innovation, equity, and meaningful impact in the social sector. We welcome candidates of all backgrounds, identities, and experiences to apply.

jobs.description:
About Command|Link

Command|Link is a global SaaS Platform providing network, voice services, and IT security solutions, helping corporations consolidate their core infrastructure into a single vendor and layering on a proprietary single pane of glass platform. Command|Link has revolutionized the IT industry by tackling the problems our competitors create. In recognition for our unprecedented innovation and dedication, Command|Link was recognized as the SD-WAN Product of the Year, ITSM Visionary Spotlight, UCaaS Product of the Year, NaaS Product of the Year, Supplier of the Year, and the AT&T Strategic Growth Partner. Command|Link has built the only IT platform for scale that solves ISP vendor sprawl and IT headaches. We make it easy for our customers to get more done, maximize uptime and improve the bottom line.

Learn more about us here!

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the following states: Alabama, Arizona, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Indiana, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maryland, Michigan, Mississippi, Missouri, Nevada, New Hampshire, North Carolina, Ohio, Oklahoma, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Virginia, Wisconsin

About your new role:

CommandLink's vendor ecosystem is the backbone of how we deliver connectivity and services to our customers, and this role will own the relationship between CommandLink and our vendors from the data side up. Today our team manages a large volume of vendor information that constantly needs to be tracked, verified, and updated across our systems, starting with our Quote Tool, which holds the most complete picture we have of each vendor and client. Keeping that tool accurate and current is critical to how the whole business operates.

We're looking for a Vendor Operations Analyst who doesn't just plan around the data, but who gets into the platform and does the work: tracking down information, entering it into the system, and analyzing it to surface insights. You'll work hands on with vendor and platform data every day, and you'll be a key point of contact for vendors, Sales, and other internal stakeholders. This isn't a deeply technical role, but it does require someone analytical, comfortable navigating systems and tools, and confident enough to bring a commercial mindset to every conversation.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Own and maintain the Quote Tool, rate cards, and building lists/zip codes, making sure they always hold the most complete and accurate vendor and client information possible, and work toward a single source of truth for all vendor data.
  • Acquire vendor information (building lists, rate cards, API capabilities, contact and escalation matrices), load it into the Platform, SharePoint, Quote Tool, and Executed Contracts folder, and keep budgetary versus firm quoting set up and up to date.
  • Analyze platform data to identify trends and generate insights (win rates, where and why we're losing deals by customer, region, or vendor), build vendor scorecards, report on quote tool results, and track KPIs.
  • Partner with Sales and Regional Pricing Analysts to shape strategy by region, for example onboarding more vendors, adjusting portfolio in a given country, or using budgetary quoting.
  • Work with the Dev team on vendor API onboarding and maintenance, test serviceability and pricing, run monthly proactive testing once new integrations go live, and make sure key vendors' APIs are running correctly.
  • Serve as the point of contact for US vendor escalations, platform escalations, and vendor portal access for new joiners, and support MSA revisions and adjustments as needed.
  • Lead the project to have vendors submit their own onboarding updates, building lists, and rate cards directly.
  • Takes on additional responsibilities and projects as needed to support the success of the team and organization.

What you'll need for success:

Required

  • Experience with Sales and/or purchasing/buyer functions; strong Excel skills.
  • A hands on, analytical profile: comfortable working directly with platform data, not just planning around it, but tracking it down and entering it into the system yourself.
  • A commercial mindset; you're just as comfortable talking to vendors as you are to Sales or other internal stakeholders.
  • Proactive by nature; you go get the information you need rather than waiting for it to come to you.
  • A self starter who thrives in fast paced environments; startup or high growth company experience is a plus.
  • Comfortable learning and navigating systems and tools quickly. No deep technical or engineering background required, but you should understand how the platform works and why.

Nice to Have

  • Background in telecom, IT services, or B2B SaaS pricing structures.

Why you'll love life at Command|Link

Join us at CommandLink, where you'll have the opportunity to shape the future of business communication. We value the innovative spirit and seek individuals ready to bring their unique vision and expertise to a team that values bold ideas and strategic thinking. Are you ready to make an impact?

  • Room to grow at a high-growth company
  • An environment that celebrates ideas and innovation
  • Your work will have a tangible impact
  • Generous Medical, Dental, and Vision coverage for full-time employees
  • Flexible time off
  • 401k to help you save for the future
  • Fun events at cool locations
  • Free DoorDash lunches on Fridays
  • Employee referral bonuses to encourage the addition of great new people to the team

Commandlink hires individuals in a number of geographic regions and the pay ranges listed reflect the cost of labor across these regions. The base pay for this position as displayed at the bottom of the job description is a range based on our lowest geographic region, up to our highest geographic region. These tools support our recruiting team by identifying qualifications and experience that align with the requirements of each role.

AnewHealth is one of the nation’s leading pharmacy care management companies that specializes in caring for people with the most complex, chronic needs—wherever they call home. We enable better outcomes for patients and the healthcare organizations who support them. Established in 2023 through the combination of ExactCare and Tabula Rasa HealthCare, we provide a suite of solutions that includes comprehensive pharmacy services; full-service pharmacy benefit management; and specialized support services for Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly. With over 1,400 team members, we care for more than 100,000 people across all 50 states.

Job Details

The CareKinesis Clinical Initiatives Pharmacist utilizes clinical knowledge and skills coupled with innovative technology to optimize medication regimens and prevent adverse events for participants by identifying and rectifying medication-related problems, empowering participants to actively participate in their own clinical decision-making, and collaborating with providers, pharmacists, and other healthcare providers to improve outcomes.

Responsibilities

  • Conduct comprehensive and targeted Medication Safety Reviews (MSRs) for PACE participants using proprietary clinical platforms, developing individualized, measurable, and goal-oriented therapeutic care plans.

  • Complete medication reviews and reconciliation activities for new enrollments, annual and significant change assessments, care transitions, and other high-risk clinical events to support safe and effective medication use.

  • Identify, evaluate, document, and facilitate the resolution of medication-related problems, including polypharmacy, adverse drug events, potentially inappropriate medications, therapeutic gaps, adherence challenges, and medication access barriers.

  • Collaborate with providers, interdisciplinary team (IDT) members, and other healthcare professionals to communicate clinical recommendations, including medication optimization, deprescribing opportunities, and goals-of-care aligned interventions when appropriate.

  • Engage with providers through written medication safety reviews, clinical consultations, polypharmacy assessments, fall risk evaluations, and care transition reviews, while monitoring and documenting outcomes and progress toward established therapeutic goals.

  • Monitor participants receiving high-risk medications or managing complex chronic disease regimens, ensuring timely follow-up, intervention, and documentation of clinical findings and recommendations.

  • Participate in client meetings, interdisciplinary discussions, Pharmacy and Therapeutics (P&T) Committee meetings, drug utilization review activities, quality improvement initiatives, and educational programs as assigned.

  • Maintain compliance with all applicable federal and state regulations, accreditation standards, and organizational policies governing pharmacy practice, including requirements related to quality assurance, HIPAA, Fraud, Waste and Abuse (FWA), and patient safety reporting.

The above essential functions are representative of major duties of positions in this job classification. Specific duties and responsibilities may vary based upon departmental needs. Other duties may be assigned similar to the above consistent with knowledge, skills and abilities required for the job. Not all of the duties may be assigned to a position.

Qualifications: These represent the desired qualifications of the ideal candidate. They are not meant to limit consideration for candidates who do not meet all of the standards listed. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Education

  • Graduate of a pharmacy program accredited by the Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education (ACPE) or a program outside the U.S. that qualifies the individual to practice in the jurisdiction.

  • A current, active license/registration in good standing with the state board of pharmacy where practice will occur.

  • Active Board of Pharmacy Specialties (BPS) certification in geriatrics (BCGP) preferred.

Experience

  • Experience in direct contact with prescribers and patients is preferred.

  • Experience or strong interest in clinical pharmacogenomics is preferred.

  • Above-average knowledge of geriatric pharmacotherapy and ability to apply knowledge to clinical practice including (1) focusing on the special needs of older patients who may have concurrent illnesses taking multiple medications and (2) resolve complex medication-related issues that arise in the geriatric patient population.

  • Strong analytical skills with good clinical judgement and decision making including the ability to effectively and efficiently identify and rectify medication-related problems.

  • Self-motivated and eager to develop clinically and professionally with a high degree of ownership for tasks and self-accountability and strong follow-through.

Skills & Abilities

  • Ability to communicate effectively and professionally through written, verbal (e.g., face-to-face, telephonically and/or virtual communication platforms), and interpersonal skills as applied when interacting with employees, patients, healthcare professionals, clients, or agency representatives; successfully conveying and exchanging information at an appropriate level and in a positive and timely manner.

  • Strong technical and computer skills to navigate proprietary and other pharmacy software and the initiative to propose suggestions to improve operations and proprietary system development and enhancements.

  • Demonstrated experience with problem-solving, conflict resolution, and project management skills.

  • Detail oriented and organized with the ability to work with a sense of urgency, work under pressure, multi-task, and achieve deadlines without sacrificing quality.

  • Strong analytical skills with good clinical judgement and decision making including (1) the ability to effectively and efficiently identify and rectify medication-related problems, and (2) assess patients using verbal and/or visual cues, when appropriate.

  • Knowledge of state and federal laws and regulations, including HIPAA and Fraud, Waste, and Abuse.

Schedule: This is a full-time position with an expectation to work an average of 40 hours per week and be available outside of normal business hours to meet customer expectations on an ad-hoc basis. Job Description:

The Senior API Integration Consultant is a technical, client- and vendor-facing role responsible for guiding contracted third-party vendors from agreement through live production use of NextGen Enterprise APIs. The role provides hands-on technical consultation across FHIR, REST, enterprise APIs, authentication, and healthcare data workflows and translates vendor use cases into supported integrations with NextGen EHR and practice-management solutions.

The Senior API Integration Consultant leads vendor engagements through onboarding, application development, sandbox validation, beta implementation, client authorization, production readiness, and go-live. This position delivers billable Professional Services activation engagements that contribute to API program revenue, vendor time-to-production, client integration outcomes, and scalable onboarding practices.
  • Serve as the technical lead for contracted third-party vendors throughout API onboarding, application development, sandbox testing, beta implementation, client authorization, and production go-live.
  • Deliver billable Professional Services activation engagements, including structured production-readiness reviews, route and tier preflight checks, beta-client readiness assessments, gap-remediation plans, and time-boxed beta launch sprints.
  • Provide hands-on technical consultation on FHIR, REST and JSON APIs, web services, authentication, SMART application launch, Bulk FHIR, and modern integration patterns.
  • Evaluate vendor use cases and data requirements and map them to supported API routes, FHIR resources, and NextGen EHR, practice-management, and clinical workflows.
  • Identify API coverage gaps, technical risks, and integration blockers and coordinate appropriate resolution or escalation through Product, Engineering, Support, and program channels.
  • Manage each vendor engagement as a technical project, including scope, milestones, timelines, dependencies, deliverables, launch-blocker triage, and stakeholder communications.
  • Coordinate client-environment readiness, consent and authorization requirements, testing activities, downtime and cutover planning, and rollback considerations among vendors, clients, and internal teams.
  • Prioritize contracted vendors that have not yet reached production by evaluating readiness, dependencies, risk, and business impact and driving each engagement toward a defined next milestone.
  • Ensure activation services are delivered consistently to similarly situated vendors and in alignment with established program, contractual, regulatory, and Professional Services requirements.
  • Partner with Business Development, Support, Product, Engineering, Client Success, Sales, and other internal teams to resolve blockers and align on vendor go-live outcomes.
  • Track engagement time, deliverables, milestones, and outcomes to support accurate Professional Services billing, utilization reporting, and API program revenue objectives.
  • Develop and improve enablement materials, technical documentation, readiness tools, and repeatable playbooks that reduce onboarding friction and support program scalability.
  • Provide feedback to Product and program leadership regarding recurring technical blockers, API route gaps, vendor needs, and process improvements that affect time-to-production and client integration outcomes.
  • Support production-scale adoption and stabilization of newly activated vendor integrations, as assigned.
  • Perform other duties that support the overall objective of the position.

Education Required:

  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, health informatics, information systems, or a related field.

Experience Required:

  • 6+ years of progressive experience in technical integration, API or software integration, solution consulting, implementation consulting, or Professional Services within a healthcare technology or SaaS environment.
  • 3+ years of hands-on experience working with RESTful APIs, FHIR, HL7, web services, authentication protocols, and modern integration practices.
  • Experience independently leading complex technical integration engagements from initial discovery and solution mapping through testing, production readiness, and go-live.
  • Experience working directly with third-party vendors, developers, clients, or partners to resolve technical issues and deliver integrations into production environments.
  • Experience with NextGen Enterprise EHR and practice-management solutions or a comparable healthcare technology platform, including clinical, administrative, and revenue-cycle data workflows.
  • Experience evaluating technical requirements, identifying integration gaps and risks, and determining appropriate remediation or escalation paths.
  • Experience managing multiple concurrent technical engagements, including scope, timelines, dependencies, deliverables, priorities, and stakeholder expectations.
  • Experience coordinating technical work across Product, Engineering, Support, Client Success, Sales, or comparable cross-functional teams.
  • Experience developing technical documentation, readiness assessments, implementation plans, gap-remediation plans, or repeatable delivery processes.
  • Experience delivering billable consulting or Professional Services engagements preferred.

License/Certification Required:

  • Project management, healthcare interoperability, cloud, integration, or other relevant technical certification preferred.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:

  • Knowledge of: RESTful APIs, JSON, web services, OAuth 2.0, token-based authentication, and secure integration patterns. Healthcare interoperability standards and frameworks, including FHIR, HL7, USCDI, SMART application launch, and Bulk FHIR. EHR and practice-management data structures and associated clinical, administrative, and revenue-cycle workflows. API onboarding and activation processes, including sandbox testing, beta implementation, client authorization, production readiness, cutover, and stabilization. Software development lifecycle, testing, troubleshooting, technical readiness assessment, and data-access scoping. Applicable healthcare interoperability, privacy, data-access, and regulatory requirements. Technical project delivery and billable Professional Services practices.
  • Skill in: Leading complex vendor and client API integrations from onboarding through production go-live. Translating business use cases, data requirements, and workflows into supported API and interoperability solutions. Assessing production readiness and diagnosing API, authentication, data-access, workflow, and environment-related issues. Identifying technical risks, dependencies, and launch blockers and developing appropriate remediation or escalation plans. Managing concurrent technical engagements, priorities, timelines, deliverables, and stakeholder expectations.
  • Communicating complex technical information to technical and non-technical audiences. Developing technical documentation, readiness assessments, gap-remediation plans, and repeatable delivery playbooks. Coordinating technical issue resolution across internal and external stakeholders.
  • Ability to: Independently guide contracted vendors from onboarding through live production use of NextGen Enterprise APIs. Exercise judgment in evaluating technical readiness, risks, gaps, and appropriate resolution or escalation paths. Balance multiple vendor engagements, competing priorities, dependencies, and business commitments. Adapt integration approaches to differing vendor use cases, client environments, and technical constraints. Deliver consistent, high-quality billable services in accordance with program, contractual, and regulatory requirements. Influence outcomes and collaborate effectively across technical, business, client, and vendor stakeholders. Identify recurring issues and recommend improvements that reduce vendor time-to-production and support program scalability.

JOB SUMMARY

We are seeking a highly skilled, technically proficient and detail-oriented Principal Mechanical Engineer with expertise in metal structures, frame design, and fabrication to support the development of power and cooling infrastructure for data centers. This role is critical in designing robust mechanical systems that house and support electrical and thermal management equipment, ensuring structural integrity, manufacturability, and compliance with industry standards.

LOCATION

India - Remote

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Experience designing and integrating hydronic systems including pumps, piping networks, valves, and heat exchangers for data center cooling applications.
  • Knowledge of fluid dynamics, pressure drop calculations, and pipe sizing for chilled water and glycol-based systems.
  • Understanding of installation constraints, maintenance access, and serviceability in large-scale mechanical infrastructure.
  • Design and develop mechanical frames, enclosures, and support structures for data center power and cooling products (e.g., UPS systems, battery racks, CRAC units, containment systems, LVS, MVS).

  • Create detailed CAD models and fabrication drawings, including weldments, sheet metal, and machined parts.

  • Collaborate with electrical, thermal, and systems engineering teams to integrate mechanical designs with functional components.
  • Lead mechanical design reviews and contribute to cross-functional design validation efforts.
  • Develop and maintain design documentation including BOMs, specifications, test plans, and engineering change orders (ECOs).
  • Drive continuous improvement in mechanical design for manufacturability (DFM), cost reduction, and performance optimization.
  • Interface with suppliers and customers to resolve fabrication issues and ensure quality standards are met.
  • Support lifecycle management of mechanical components, including obsolescence planning and alternate sourcing.
  • Conduct root cause analysis and corrective actions for mechanical failures or field issues.
  • Ensure mechanical designs support airflow management, thermal containment, and integration with cooling systems (e.g., in-row cooling, rear door heat exchangers).

  • Creative, self-motivated, accountable, and team-oriented

  • Skilled in writing reports, business correspondence, and procedural guides
  • Effective at presenting information and responding to management, clients, and public queries
  • Capable of influencing others and sharing best practices
  • Comfortable working as part of a global team
  • Capable of assessing projects, articulating risks, and developing project milestones

  • Able to mentor less experienced engineers
